blocks.content: Article 32 is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.

items: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) added three new words to the Preamble: 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'.
Joint Sitting of Parliament under Article 108 is summoned by the President but presided over by the Speaker of Lok Sabha.
Money Bills under Article 110 can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha with the prior recommendation of the President.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th November 1949 and came into full effect on 26th January 1950.
Article 32 guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies and was called the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
The Preamble has been amended only once by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.
Right to Property was deleted from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, and made a constitutional right under Article 300A.
Fundamental Duties were added under Part IV-A (Article 51A) upon the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
